msItem.title: Glossed Gospels
msItem.incipit: Nomen libri euangelium grece bonum nuncium

msItem.title: Canon law formularies
msItem.incipit: H. dei gratia abbas illius loci B. clerico salutem
msItem.note: Five leaves with law formularies, which contain models for letters, sentences, donations, etc.; integral to the quire containing the end of the text of Matthew.
References to Oxford and its churches (St Frideswide, St Peter, Mary, Osney, and Thame); dates 1193, 1194, 1199, and 1203; Kings Richard and John as well as Pope Innocent III are mentioned.
msItem.bibl: Extracts printed in Salter, Pantin, and Richardson (273–277).

msItem.title: Sermons for the liturgy
msItem.note: Sermons for Christmas day, Easter, Pentecost, and the beginning of Lent.
Nos. 3 and 5–7 below occur in a similar grouping in Oxford, Balliol College, MS 240.

msItem.incipit: Hodie fratres karissimi redemptor noster ad nos uenit per uterum intermerate uirginis. et fieri dignatus est homo ut hominem redimeret.
msItem.explicit: Et ideo fratres karissimi mundemus illi corda nostra ut hodie cum ad nostram salutem uenerit recipi mereamur. et cum ipso intrare in gaudium eternum. Quod ipse prestare dignetur cui est honor et gloria in secula seculorum. Amen.
msItem.note: Also found in Troyes, Médiathèque, ms. 1771, fol. 118v; Zürich, Zentralbibliothek, Rh. 90, p. 60; Padova, Biblioteca Antoniana, MS 473, fols 167v–168r.

msItem.incipit: Pascha nostrum immolatus est cristus. 1 Cor. 5:7 Si igitur pascha cristus est pensandum nobis est quid de pascha lex loquitur. ut uiteatur subtilius quomodo de cristo dictum uideatur.
msItem.explicit: Nemini imple reliceat⹎ quod male inchoat⹎ ne ad amorem dei pigri simus adiuuet ipse quod amamus ihesus cristus dominus noster. qui uiuit et regnat.

msItem.author: Maximus of Turin
msItem.title: Sermones
msItem.incipit: Legimus in prophetis. Cum niniue ciuitatis subuersio imineret. et iuxta sententiam dei destruendam illam tempus irrueret⹎ quod consistentes in ea aliud non habuisse praesidium nisi ut (fol. 206v) abiectis copiosis epulis. ieiunia continuata susciperent. et diuitiarum ambitione deposita paupertate induerent et humilitate.
msItem.explicit: De quo nos dominus per prophetam prtatur et amonet dicens. Frange esurienti panem tuum etc. Is. 58:7 Quod in nobis implete dignetur saluator mundi. qui cum deo patre. etc.

msItem.author: Geoffroy Babion
msItem.title: Sermones
msItem.incipit: Verbo domini celi firmati sunt. et spiritu oris eius omnis uirtus eorum. Ps. 32:6 Fratres karissimi scire debetis que et quanta sit sollempnitas ista et quare per omnes ecclesias uniuersaliter celebratur.
msItem.explicit: Contra ergo talem consolatorem cordis hospicia preparemus uirtutibus ornemus. a uiciis mundemus ut eum digne suscipere mereamur. Qui uiuit et regnat.

msItem.author: Caesarius of Arles
msItem.title: Sermones
msItem.incipit: Precauendum in omnibus bona opera exercentibus fratres karissimi quod dominus dicit in euangelio. Attendite ne iustitiam uestram eorum hominibus etc. Matt. 6:1 Hec lectio sancti euangelii fratres karissimi uidetur michi quod secundum litteras non potest intellegi. et ideo deo auxiliante requiramus qualiter ad eius sensum spiritualem peruenire possimus.
msItem.explicit: Sed pro dei amore et desiderio eterne uite beatitudinis faciamus. Quod nobis prestare.

msItem.author: Pseudo-Augustine
msItem.title: Sermones ad fratres in eremo commorantes
msItem.incipit: Audite filioli mei et intelligite quomodo sacra scriptura nos ammonet ad regna celorum innitat et uiam ostendit quomodo mala mundi huius euadere possimus et ad uitam eternam cristo adiuuante peruenire.
msItem.explicit: Hec precepta implendi uirtutem nobis prestare dignetur. saluator mundi qui cum patre. et spiritu sancto. etc.

msItem.incipit: Primum omnium. Mark 12:29 tria quedam unicuique homini pernecessaria sunt. fides. spes. caritas.
msItem.explicit: Tercia delinquante corrigere et errantes⹎ reducere in uia ueritatis. Hec in nobis implere dignetur saluator mundi⹎ qui cum deo patre et spiritu sancto uiuit et regnat.

binding.p: Christopher Clarkson described this as an important binding in the evolution from the tab-period (Randall, 175); it may be possible to link this to the manuscript’s provenance with further research.

history.provenance: Quaritch (no. 49) argued, the original scribe has added a large number of ecclesiastical forms, citations, deeds of bequest, etc., and although intended to be blank forms a large number of them have been copied from original charters of S. Frideswide, Oxford (now Christ Church), S. Frideswide, Oseney, and S. Peter’s in the East, Oxford. The forms belonging to first named church are in the majority, and therefore I think that the volame probably emanated from the monastery attached to S. Frideswide, Oxford. Ker and Watson rejected this on the basis that the documents do not in themselves prove the book’s origin or provenance. Campbell (35–6) was unaware of the earlier attribution and made a similar case for associating the book with the Augustinian priory of St Frideswide or Osney Abbey on the basis of the number of regular canons featuring in its formulary, viewing the former as more likely because there is more evidence of the priors of St Frideswide’s serving as papal judge-delegates.

provenance.orgName: Reading, Berkshire, Benedictine abbey of Saint Mary the Virgin
provenance.p: All known books owned by both Reynoldes and Fitton have a Reading provenance; attributed to Reading by Randall (174), following a suggestion of Michael Gullick on the evidence of the manuscript’s later provenance (citing Coates, 133, 200, 208).

history.provenance: J. Reynoldes (or D. S. Reynoldes?), seventeenth century; his ownership inscription, left pastedown and fol. 3r.
Thomas Fitton of Siddington (d. 1599): inscribed, fol. 3r.
Rowland Clegg-Hill, Third Viscount of Hawkstone Park, Shropshire (1833–1895); his ex libris and pencil notation on left pastedown.
Bernard Quaritch, booksellers, London, catalogue 344 (1916), no. 49.
Guiseppe Martini, booksellers, New York (later Lugano), catalogue 13 (1916), no. 11.
history.acquisition: Walters Art Museum, 1931, by Henry Walters’ bequest.
